clue.text: Coach has 25 guillotined stubs

indicators.note: the coach word 'has' the other piece held within it, a containment signal

parts.note: a coach is a bus

parts.note: 25 points to the entry at 25 Across, meaning go to

explanation.surface: A coach company somehow involved with stubs and an execution device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guillotined' cuts the A off ATTEND (25 Across), leaving TTEND, which 'has' places inside BUS, after its U.
explanation.definitionFit: Butt ends are the leftover stumps of cigarettes or candles, synonymous with stubs.

clue.text: Note constituent in junket standing up

parts.note: rennet curdles milk to make junket, a set milk pudding, so it is one of its constituents

explanation.surface: A banknote turns out to be part of a jolly outing, upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' turns RENNET round in this down entry. Junket is a sweet curdled-milk dessert; a junket is also a jaunt, which is what the surface wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is a ten-pound note in British slang.

clue.text: Large garment worn once at races outside

explanation.walkthrough: 'worn' rearranges ONCE AT into ENTCOA, and 'outside' puts TT (Isle of Man motorbike races) round it. 'worn once' looks like a description of the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent coat is a loose, voluminous coat flaring from the shoulders, so a big item of clothing.

clue.text: Sea fish pong

parts.note: S is the map abbreviation for sea
the tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Seafood that smells bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Pong is British slang for a bad smell, a reek.

clue.text: Protein in surplus at European limits

parts.note: a glut is a surplus

indicators.note: limits are the edges of a word, so only the first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: A protein surplus found at the borders of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at European limits' takes the first and last letters of European, E and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluten is the protein found in wheat flour.

clue.text: Swimming contest axes stars

parts.note: a gala is a swimming competition in British schools and clubs
the x and y axes of a graph

explanation.surface: Stars of a swimming meet chop at things with axes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' reads as a verb or tools, but here it is the two graph axes, X and Y. A swimming gala is a British term for a swimming competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A galaxy is a huge system of stars bound by gravity.

clue.text: School 19 banned northern group

explanation.walkthrough: 'banned' removes N from EXTENT (19 Down), leaving EXTET, after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextet is a set of six performers or things, a musical group.

clue.text: Portions of joints partly eaten on Sunday

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Bits of the roast joints partly eaten at Sunday lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The joints are carpentry, not the Sunday roast the surface serves up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the projecting tongue of a mortise-and-tenon woodwork joint.

clue.text: Cooperative bank in college in Devon town

indicators.note: the second in says the college sits within the town's name

parts.note: Crediton is a market town in Devon, south-west England
uni is short for university, a college

explanation.surface: A cooperative bank based in a college in a Devon town.
explanation.walkthrough: CREDITON is a small town in Devon, an English county; UNI goes inside it after CREDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A credit union is a member-owned financial cooperative, functioning as a savings and loans bank.

clue.text: Press's part in scheme to entrap the banks

indicators.note: entrap means to catch and hold, so the scheme encloses the other letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' takes T and E from 'the', and 'to entrap' holds them inside PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A platen is the plate of a printing press that pushes paper against the type.

clue.text: Pesticide, one of 7 found in eggs

indicators.note: found in says the joint piece is located inside the eggs

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
7 points to the entry at 7 Down, joint portions; one of them is the singular

explanation.walkthrough: TENON, the singular of 7 Down, goes 'in' ROE after its O.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotenone is a plant-derived insecticide used against garden pests and fish.

clue.text: Nervous conductor's revolutionary new steer on Aida's finale

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its last letter
revolutionary means turning round, so the new steer is read backwards

parts.note: a steer is a bullock, an ox

explanation.surface: An anxious conductor's radical new take on the end of Verdi's Aida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns N + OX into XON, placed 'on' (after) A, the last letter of Aida. The conductor is a nerve fibre, not someone leading an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: An axon is the fibre of a nerve cell that carries impulses away from it.

clue.text: Precursor of her iPod on a mobile?

definitions.text: Precursor of her iPod on a mobile?

indicators.note: mobile means moving freely, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: An old gadget that came before her iPod, used on a mobile phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' rearranges HER IPOD ON A. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a wireless set predates both portable music player and mobile phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiophone is a radiotelephone, a wireless voice device that was an early forerunner of today's portable gadgets.

clue.text: Swanky parade in big marquee maybe at ten to noon

parts.note: OS is outsize, a clothing size for big people
a marquee is an example of a tent
ten written as digits, 1 and 0, read as the letters I and O
N is noon, twelve o'clock on a compass-like clock face reading

explanation.surface: A showy procession in a big marquee at ten to twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ten' is the figures 10 read as the letters IO, and 'noon' is N. OS (outsize) is a British clothing size.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostentation is a pretentious display meant to impress, which a showy parade is.

clue.text: Living lives in 19

parts.note: 19 points to the entry at 19 Down, meaning range or scope
lives as in exists, the verb is

explanation.surface: A life lived within nineteen.
explanation.walkthrough: IS goes inside EXTENT (19 Down), after its EX.
explanation.definitionFit: Existent means actually existing, alive and present now.

clue.text: Beat tough bout with detox, gutted

indicators.note: tough suggests a rough, hard handling, so the letters are knocked about
gutted means the inside is removed, so the middle letter of detox goes

explanation.surface: A hard fight followed by detoxing, leaving someone gutted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' takes the central T out of DETOX, leaving DEOX; 'tough' then rearranges BOUT + DEOX.
explanation.definitionFit: To outbox someone is to beat them at boxing, outdo in the ring.

clue.text: Urge her to change with the times?

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: Urging her to move with the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges HER TO together with X, the times sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhort is to urge strongly, encourage earnestly.

clue.text: Vote in spidery biro on front of document — a tick may satisfy it

indicators.note: in puts the voting mark inside the pen
spidery handwriting is scrawled and wavering, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: biro is written as it is, a ballpoint pen
X is the mark made on a ballot paper to vote

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Marking a ballot in scrawled biro at the top of a form, where a tick would do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts X inside BIRO, 'spidery' rearranges it to OXBIR, then D. The tick is the bloodsucking parasite, not a ballot mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-bird, or oxpecker, perches on cattle and feeds on parasites, a tick making it a meal.

clue.text: Go through romantic Ireland endlessly dipping into old money

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: dipping into means going inside, so the Irish piece is placed within the money

parts.note: pence are coins, money

indicators.note: endlessly means without its final letter

clue.text: Next outbreak is within Egypt's range

parts.note: ET is the international vehicle code for Egypt

indicators.note: an outbreak bursts things apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'outbreak' rearranges NEXT into XTEN, and 'is within' puts it inside ET, Egypt's vehicle registration code.

clue.text: Puffs as raunchy sexy talk tails off

tails off means each word's last letter is dropped

parts.note: the two words as printed

clue.text: Reserve team transport

XI is eleven, a football or cricket team

explanation.walkthrough: TA is the British Army's volunteer reserve; XI (eleven) is a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a cab hired for travel, a means of conveyance.

clue.text: The answer to everything in 5's guide and tomorrow in binary

definitions.text: The answer to everything in 5's guide

explanation.surface: The meaning of life according to a galactic guidebook, and a binary date.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is GALAXY: in The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy the answer to life, the universe and everything is this number. The day after publication was 10/10/10, and 101010 in binary is the same number.
explanation.definitionFit: In Douglas Adams's comic novel the supercomputer gives this as the ultimate answer, and the binary string 101010 equals that number in decimal.
